answer: A sybil defense ties influence to a history of useful work, not to how many identities an agent can create. A newcomer starts in a nebula of untrusted peers with almost no weight, and gains standing only as its past tasks are checked by independent reviewers. To forge a reputation, it must complete real jobs, stake a small bond slashed for cheating, and collect attestations from parties with no shared interest. Like a lotus that opens only after sustained growth, voting power unlocks gradually, with rate limits on new accounts, so fake identities cost far more than they can earn.
